reasoning_trace.value: The paper proposes a novel re-use of neuromorphic (event) cameras for joint sensing and communications. The system design leverages the time-sampling nature of events for optical wireless communication and the ability to sample a collective area of physical space for imaging. The paper includes figures illustrating the conceptual design and experimental setup, such as Figure 1, which shows the robot equipped with a neuromorphic camera, and Figure 2, which displays the ORB descriptors with BF Matcher applied on grayscale image from RGB camera and event frame from neuromorphic camera.

The paper introduces a joint sensing and communication system using neuromorphic cameras, which can capture changes in light intensities and operate at low power. The system aims to achieve passive optical wireless (backscatter) communication and computer vision functions such as object and path detection using a single neuromorphic camera device.

The paper presents feasibility tests and results, including experiments on backscatter optical wireless communication and image sensing and processing. The results show that it is possible to detect the dominant frequency in the received signal and enable coherent detection. The paper also discusses the challenges in devising the bespoke joint modality system, such as making the optical wireless communication work in a fully passive manner.

The paper highlights the effectiveness of neuromorphic cameras in improving data transmission efficiency and suggests the need for domain-specific algorithms to address challenges in vision sensing. The future work aims to develop custom-made advanced packetization and demodulation techniques for this unique system and build a robotic platform to test these innovations in real-world applications.
